condition-number.def: For a matrix \(A\), the ratio of its largest to its smallest stretch (for symmetric \(A\), \(\lambda_{\max}/\lambda_{\min}\)). Large \(\kappa(A)\) means solving \(A\mathbf x=\mathbf b\) loses about \(\log_{10}\kappa\) digits, and gradient descent on a quadratic with Hessian \(A\) is slow.

finite-difference.def: Estimate a derivative from the function alone: \(\frac{f(\beta+h)-f(\beta-h)}{2h}\). Used to check a hand-derived gradient.

hessian.def: The matrix of second partial derivatives of a loss. For the MSE of linear regression it is \(\frac2n\bX\T\bX\); its eigenvalues are the curvatures of the loss bowl.

learning-rate.def: The step size \(\eta\) in gradient descent, \(\bbeta\leftarrow\bbeta-\eta\nabla L\). On a quadratic loss it must be below \(2/\lambda_{\max}\) of the Hessian, or the steps grow and training diverges.

loss-curve.def: A plot of the training loss against the step number, usually with a log y-axis. The first thing to look at when training any model.

polynomial-features.def: Extra columns \(x^2, x^3,\dots\) added to the design matrix so that a model that is linear in its coefficients can fit a curve.

relative-error.def: \(|g_{\text{num}}-g_{\text{ana}}|/(|g_{\text{num}}|+|g_{\text{ana}}|)\): a scale-free comparison of two gradients. Below about \(10^{-6}\) means the analytic gradient is right.

standardise.def: Replace each feature by \(z=(x-m)/s\), using the mean \(m\) and standard deviation \(s\) of the training rows, so every feature is on the same scale.

train-test-split.def: Shuffle the rows (with a fixed seed) and hold some back as a test set that is never used for fitting, so the test error estimates performance on new data.
